The key is accepted only through a non-echoing hidden prompt and never appears in argv/env/registry/transcript/logs/stdout/the JSON result; the wrapper refuses to run under transcription or Verbose/Debug tracing.

Independent adversarial review (all listed vectors): NO CRITICAL, NO HIGH. The ACL construction, secret scrubbing (finally runs on exit; BSTR zeroed; SecureString disposed), fail-closed validations, TOCTOU-safe File.Move overwrite-refusal, and no-task-mutation/no-network/no-#48 were confirmed sound. THREE improvements applied in response: (A) functional fix - the tenant is granted Modify (read+write+delete), not a bare Read, so the one-use consumer (run_oneshot_attest, running AS guvfx_u_46) can actually overwrite+delete/shred the key (a Read-only grant would have silently left the secret on disk); (B) MEDIUM-1 - all test seams are now refused in production behind a self-test signal the production launch path never sets (test_seam_in_production), so the fail-closed contract cannot be bypassed from argv; (C) MEDIUM-2 - the reparse chain is re-verified immediately before the write (closing a junction planted during the human-input window) and a directory the wrapper creates is given an admin-owned protected ACL (tenant traverse-only). Residual LOWs documented: Windows cannot forensically wipe a deleted file (bounded-lifetime guarantee, not secure-erase); the destination bundle directory is an admin-created deployment precondition. Regression tests added for each fix.

SetOwner to Administrators is best-effort (needs SeRestorePrivilege); the verifier accepts an owner in {SYSTEM, Administrators, the tenant SID} so a non-elevated owner does not weaken the DACL guarantee.

Windows storage cannot promise a forensic overwrite of a deleted file; the guarantee is bounded ephemeral lifetime + restrictive ACLs + one-use consumer deletion + mandatory cleanup, documented in the script and ADR.
